title: Priv EKS provisioner: verification pipeline, safe-controlplane upgrades, and proactive health bridge
creator: Asha Menon
description: Implement a hardened Terraform module and accompanying runbook/workflow that provisions Redwood Private control planes (EKS) with: automated preflight validations, a canary-style control-plane upgrade orchestration, continuous health probes, and a verification pipeline that detects and auto-remediates common drift/upgrade regressions. This ticket covers module interfaces, upgrade orchestration hooks, health-check probes (apiserver latency/error budget, etc.), Terraform-driven remediation primitives, CI verification jobs, and docs/operational runbooks.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module exposes configurable variables: control_plane_version, kms_key_arn, cluster_networking (cidr, subnets), bootstrap_iam_role_arn, node_pool_defaults, maintenance_window, upgrade_strategy (canary|rolling|bluegreen), and health_probe_profile
Provisioned cluster in private VPC via CI (non-prod) with module returns stable outputs for kubeconfig, control_plane_endpoint, and audit_log_s3_path

Control plane upgrade path: canary upgrade applied to a small AZ surface area first, health probes pass for 30 minutes, then staged rollout completes without >1% API error increase or >250ms median API latency regression
Automated preflight checks run in CI and block apply when failures detected: subnet reachability, KMS key policy binding, service-linked role presence, and IAM boundary checks

Drift detector identifies changes to control plane and nodegroup tags/config within 10 minutes of drift and creates a remediation task (Terraform plan + human-approve remediation) for high-risk drift, and auto-reconciles low-risk tag drift within 30 minutes
Health bridge dashboard surfaces key signals (apiserver error rate, controller-manager restarts, manifests stuck, etc.) with alert thresholds and runbook links
Documentation includes Terraform module README, example usage for Private (VPC) deployments, upgrade runbook, and a troubleshooting checklist. Links to CI jobs and PRs included
Module tests: unit (terraform validate + tflint), integration (apply/destroy in ephemeral non-prod), and e2e upgrade test (canary -> staged upgrade) in CI all green
tasks: Define module schema and variables (owner: Liam)
Implement preflight validators as null_resource hooks with local-exec checks and explicit error messages
Add optional IAM role binding for KMS/SSM with documented minimal policies
Create upgrade orchestrator plan: terraform plan/apply strategy + small imperative controller for canary gating
Design health probe set and expose CloudWatch metrics/Prometheus exporters to Console
Implement a lightweight drift detector using remote state diff + AWS Config integration
Add CI pipelines: preflight (fast), full-apply in ephemeral env, canary-upgrade e2e test
Author runbook and module README with example usage and troubleshooting steps
Security review and threat-model for upgrade orchestration and KMS integration
notes: Design decision: prefer Terraform-native approach for initial provisioning + canary orchestration implemented as a small controller in Go. Rationale: keep majority of lifecycle declarative while enabling imperative gating during upgrades (safer than trying to encode complex canaries purely in TF apply).

Trade-offs considered: fully operator-driven control plane vs Terraform orchestrator. Operator gives more live-state control but increases long-term maintenance and security surface. We will revisit after first 2 customers in Private enroll.

Risk: applying control plane version changes can surface CRD/controller incompatibilities. Mitigation: use canary control plane with metric-based gating and automated rollback hook that reverts Terraform apply by re-applying previous version state if gating fails.

Performance target: control plane median apiserver latency < 200ms in steady state; during canary gating no more than 250ms median and <1% error increase. These will be measured by CI e2e tests and production observability dashboards.
Implementation note: use existing eksctl-compatible AMI/ami-id lookup module for node bootstrap to reduce drift across regions. Documented in README and pinned in CI manifests.
Follow-ups: integrate with Dedicated routing policies to allow customer opt-in to staged upgrades across Dedicated/Private mix (future work)
